question: Whether 0x9908B0DF is a deviation from MT19937.

addresses.name: MT19937Twist
addresses.no_signature: The state in EDI, nothing on the stack and nothing returned; register-only, as MT19937Seed.
addresses.comment: 0xAA2C80, the MT19937 state in edi, no arguments and nothing returned: the 624-word twist, run by MT19937Next and by every function that inlines a draw whenever g_random_index is zero. **This is not a faithful MT19937, and the deviations are in the bytes.** (1) The twist constant is **0x9908B0DF** - `xor edx, 0x9908b0df` at 0xAA2CE5, 0xAA2D34, 0xAA2D81 and 0xAA2DCF, the four copies of the unrolled loop - **which is MT19937's own**: this said 'not the standard 0x9908B00D', which was wrong (corrected 2026-11-07). (2) The `y >> 1` uses `sar` (0xAA2CCA, 0xAA2D19, 0xAA2D67, 0xAA2DB4), not a logical shift, so a negative y propagates its sign. (3) **The odd test is a signed remainder**, `y % 2 == 1` - `and eax, 0x80000001; jns; dec eax; or eax, 0xFFFFFFFE; inc eax; cmp eax, 1; jne` at 0xAA2CD1..0xAA2CE3 - so a y both odd and negative (remainder -1) is **not** xored with the constant; corrected 2026-11-07, this said the rest was standard. Otherwise standard: y is assembled as `((state[k] ^ x) & 0x7FFFFFFF) ^ x`, the index walks mod 0x270 (624) and the offset is 0x18C/0x18D (397). Anyone reimplementing the game's RNG - to predict a roll or to reproduce a save - must use arithmetic shifts and the signed odd test, or the sequence will not match.
addresses.revises: Comment only: 0x9908B0DF is MT19937's own constant, not a deviation; the deviations are the sar and the signed odd test.
addresses.evidence: MT19937's matrix constant a is 0x9908B0DF (Matsumoto and Nishimura, 1998); the image's xor uses it unchanged.
